title: Other wellbeing measures

draft.title: Other wellbeing measures
card: Income alone can miss poverty. A household may earn a little more than a set income line and still lack basic things such as clean water, schooling or electricity.
The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) counts what people lack across health, education and living standards. A person is counted as poor if they lack enough of these things.
The MPI gives a picture of poverty that income measures miss. It also shows which lacks are most common in a country or region, so help can be aimed at them.
Other measures, such as the Happy Planet Index, look at different parts of wellbeing. Each measure shows one view, so using several gives a fuller picture.
draft.remember: Counting what people lack shows poverty that income alone can miss.

a.q: Why does the Multidimensional Poverty Index show poverty that an income measure can miss?
opts: It counts lacks such as clean water and schooling
It records how fairly income is shared in a country
It ranks countries by their average income per person
It measures how long people live and how happy they are
a.why: The MPI counts what people lack, such as clean water, schooling or electricity, so it can show poverty even when income looks adequate. It does not rank countries by average income, which is what an income measure does.
a.clue: Think about what the MPI counts instead of money.

b.q: Families in a village in Nepal earn just above a set income line. Most have no electricity, and their children miss school. How would the MPI describe them compared with an income measure?
opts: As poor, because they lack electricity and schooling
As not poor, because they earn above the income line
As not poor, because the MPI only counts income
As poor, because the MPI ranks them by life expectancy
b.why: The MPI counts lacks such as electricity and schooling, so these families can be counted as poor. An income measure would not count them as poor, because their income is above the line, and that is the tempting wrong answer.
b.clue: The MPI looks at what people lack, not only at what they earn.

a.best: It counts lacks such as clean water and schooling

b.best: As poor, because they lack electricity and schooling

problems.detail: The card says a person is poor if they lack 'enough' things. Under the global MPI, lacking only electricity and school attendance adds up to less than the one-third cutoff, so these families would not strictly be counted as poor. The option 'As poor' states it as certain, while the why hedges with 'can be counted'. Adding a further lack, such as no clean water or poor nutrition, would make the scenario robust.

check.summary: The card and question a are accurate. Question b's scenario may not show enough lacks to pass the real MPI poverty cutoff, so consider adding another lack, such as no clean water, so the intended answer is clearly right.
